title: Multiplication as arrays
examples: Teacher, how do I use an array to show multiplication?
Can you show me an example of rows times columns?
What is the area model for multiplication?

explain.say: Today we will learn about multiplication using arrays. An array is just a picture of things in neat rows and columns.
If you have three groups of two apples, you can count them by adding two three times. This is repeated addition.
We can write repeated addition as multiplication. Three groups of two is three times two. So we write three times two.
An array shows rows and columns clearly. If you have four rows and five columns, you have four times five items.
The area model is like drawing a rectangle to help you see the multiplication. The length times the width gives the total area.

faq.q: What is the difference between repeated addition and multiplication?
faq.a: Repeated addition means adding the same number many times. Multiplication is a faster way to write that repeated addition.
asks: Why do I need to multiply instead of adding?

faq.q: How do I know which number is the rows and which is the columns?
faq.a: You can think of rows going across like lines of text. Columns go up and down like the sides of a page.
asks: Does it matter if I switch the rows and columns?
Which number comes first in the multiplication problem?

faq.q: Can I use the area model for things that are not rectangles?
faq.a: The area model works best for shapes that are straight rectangles. It helps us count items in neat lines.
asks: Is the area model only for squares?
Do I always have to draw a box?

faq.q: If I have 5 rows of 3, is it the same as 3 rows of 5?
faq.a: Yes, it is the same. Multiplication is commutative, meaning the order does not change the answer.
asks: Is the order of numbers important in multiplication?

faq.q: What is the best way to check my multiplication answer?
faq.a: You can always check your answer by drawing an array or by using repeated addition to count it out.
asks: How can I check if my multiplication is right?
What is another way to check my work?

facts: An array shows items arranged in equal rows and columns.
Repeated addition is adding the same number several times.
Multiplication is a shortcut for repeated addition.
The area model uses length times width to find total area.

quiz.say: If you have 3 rows with 4 items in each row, what is the multiplication sentence?
quiz.why: You multiply the number of rows by the number of items in each row.

wrong.0: This only adds the two numbers once, not the total amount.
wrong.1: This is only showing two groups of four, not three groups.
wrong.3: This is also correct because the order does not matter in multiplication.

quiz.say: A rectangle has 5 units for its length and 2 units for its width. What is the total area?
quiz.why: You multiply the length by the width to find the total area.

wrong.0: This incorrectly multiplies the length by itself.
wrong.1: This is just simple addition, not finding the area.
wrong.3: This is adding the length and the width together.

quiz.say: Which calculation shows 6 groups of 5 items?
quiz.why: The number of groups is the first number, and the size of each group is the second number.

wrong.1: This only adds the two numbers together.
wrong.2: This mixes multiplication with addition incorrectly.
wrong.3: This is repeated addition, but multiplication is the shorter way to write it.
